title: Pyramid — executable, bounded and understandable development

intent.statement: Agents complete authorized development through safe decisions, actual candidate-bound checks, scoped context, precise replanning and isolated collaboration; engineers understand current results and risks; retained evidence and measured whole-workflow cost support trustworthy acceptance. Maintainable module boundaries and scenario-backed command guidance control architectural and workflow overhead.

success_evidence.description: The public skill selects a dependency-safe next action, explains current blockers, and continues authorized independent work without routine approval loops.
Registered local procedures produce candidate-bound execution records; execution, semantic acceptance and actual visual review remain distinct, and false or stale success is rejected.
Role-scoped packets, bounded code retrieval and recoverable output preserve necessary decisions while reducing measured information-transfer overhead.
Current product behavior stays linked to stable requirements; create and scoped replan reuse existing procedures and preserve unaffected IDs, contracts and valid producer proof.
Task workers and read-only helpers use isolated candidates and resources; a coordinator rejects stale results, avoids duplicate review and verifies the integrated outcome.
Engineers use the existing Board, Flow and shared inspector to identify the next gate, blockers, evidence identity and limits without confusing historical acceptance with current eligibility.
A reference-aware inventory and guarded disposable-artifact procedure control growth without deleting canonical history, active/handoff proof, unresolved failures or uncertain resources.
Fixed representative real-host workloads establish correctness, actual usage, time, questions, rework, artifact growth and human decision accuracy; unavailable measurements remain unknown.

The system retains single canonical authority, compatibility, history, least authority and fail-closed transitions; no command, hook, plan or receipt grants host permission or guarantees semantic truth.

Cohesive runtime and schema modules have explicit owners and acyclic dependencies; the core facade contains no migrated business implementation, and extraction preserves public behavior, single guarded publication and historical serialized contracts.

Every current CLI command and skill has an evidence-backed actor, trigger, distinct effect and failure/recovery scenario. Default guidance exposes only the required next decision; duplicate surfaces are rationalized only after equivalence and compatibility proof, never because of zero recorded CLI calls.

Exact Context at Right Timing governs each decision. Agents receive sufficient current facts, reuse valid context and retrieve scoped detail only when needed. Relevant changes invalidate affected context. Missing facts remain explicit. No memory platform or second authority is introduced.

Extract by responsibility and change boundary, not a file-length target. Do not add project IDs, raw arguments or histories to usage collection. Removal requires scenario, substitute, safety and compatibility proof; otherwise retain or demote from routine guidance.

Exact Context at Right Timing is the design constraint for every new interface. Name its decision, actor, required facts, retrieval trigger, validity scope and recovery path. Short output must not omit changed goals, failures, authority limits or proof gaps.

Improve memory behavior by reusing existing packets, handoffs, decisions, history and source references. Keep any retrieval index disposable and rebuildable. Do not copy current state or permissions into a competing memory store; source-grounded experience is advisory.

Require deterministic checks for mechanical contracts. Keep requirement meaning, test sufficiency and visual quality as explicit agent judgments; keep new authority and material intent/risk decisions with the human or host.

Separate can-implement, can-verify and can-accept/release blockers. Continue independent authorized work using real dependencies, active claims, scopes and resources; preserve the affected join gate and failed evidence.

Apply a single change-risk policy to amend, expand and replan. Bind reviewed material to the exact candidate and observed context. Routine authorized internal decomposition does not create new authority; material goal, permission, acceptance or irreversible-risk changes require the appropriate decision.

Preserve valid supported interfaces and historical reads while documenting intentional corrective refusals for invalid plans, malformed results and unbound public agent mutations. Do not treat previously accepted invalid inputs as required compatibility.

Evaluate context correctness, omissions, stale/cross-project retrieval, repeated reads, ineffective round trips, pending questions, wall time and total actual input/cache/output cost, including retrieval/write overhead. Do not infer success from shorter fields or more modules.

decisions.question: Which development system owns the work?
decisions.choice: Extend Standalone Pyramid with deterministic policy, explicit local runner adapters and project-fit agent guidance. Keep one canonical controller.
alternatives: Run Comet and Pyramid as competing authorities
Install every researched tool as a mandatory stack
decisions.rationale: Dual authority introduces reconciliation risk and mandatory tooling adds unmeasured setup/context cost. Adopt capabilities through bounded interfaces, not product names.

decisions.question: How is the complete intent demonstrated?
decisions.choice: Baseline: local 4.2.0 plus completed Board/Flow, installed 4.1 controller, uncommitted source and pending code binding. Accept three cumulative public journeys: OUTCOME-810 trustworthy repair; OUTCOME-820 repeated change with scoped context/specs/parallelism; OUTCOME-830 qualified agent-and-engineer full lifecycle.
alternatives: Seven isolated component gates without a public journey
One horizontal backend/UI/test sequence
Treat setup or a task wave as an accepted increment
decisions.rationale: Each rung is usable and resolves a different outcome-level risk. All agreed capabilities remain required. Later gates re-establish inherited behavior; implementation may proceed ahead when it does not consume earlier work. GATE-830 already covers every requirement, so no redundant final gate is added.

decisions.question: How do we preserve parallelism and truthful dependencies?
decisions.choice: CONTRACT-801 establishes consumed interface, assurance and measurement facts. Independent adapters/policy/context/specification/delegation/Observer/retention start afterward in the same earliest wave. Integration edges constrain acceptance without serializing independent coding. Core/CLI integrations have one sequential owner.
alternatives: Require every first-increment gate before all later coding
Let all workers edit core/CLI concurrently
Persist another parallel task ledger
decisions.rationale: Actual consumption and shared executable entry edits need dependencies; an unavailable final runner or review is not a start dependency for unrelated implementation. Live conflict/resource analysis still determines actual grouping.

decisions.question: What proof and cleanup authority is accepted?
decisions.choice: Separate execution provenance, source identity, semantic/visual judgment, actual host permission and independent reviewer provenance. Preserve old proof trust and failed evidence. Cleanup requires explicit bounded authority and positive ownership/reference/process checks.
alternatives: Trust a manually submitted passed receipt
Treat any hash as independent execution proof
Automatically delete unreferenced/current-state-only evidence
decisions.rationale: Local instrumentation is not a security oracle against a malicious process. Unknown state must remain unknown, and inventory cannot grant authority.

decisions.question: How will efficiency and usability claims be qualified?
decisions.choice: Preregister baseline/candidate cases, host identities, actual usage/time/quality thresholds and human questions before evaluation. Evaluate retained successful and failed runs; unavailable accounting or people keep required measurements blocked.
alternatives: Infer savings from stdout bytes or command counts
Use only successful pairs or agent-simulated humans
Compress all language or history unconditionally
decisions.rationale: Total outcome cost and incorrect acceptance determine system value. Existing evidence does not prove savings; controlled language and fewer calls are hypotheses to test.

decisions.question: How should architectural growth be reduced without weakening authority?
decisions.choice: Extract storage, lifecycle/read-side and schema ownership through three bounded tasks; reuse existing CLI and Observer owners. Preserve thin public facades and one guarded publication boundary.
alternatives: Split at arbitrary line numbers
Move all code into a new giant module
Big-bang canonical schema migration
decisions.rationale: Responsibilities and independent failure/compatibility boundaries justify the split. Reuse current behavior and tests; no additional product gate or general framework is required.

decisions.question: Does a zero recorded usage count justify removal?
decisions.choice: No. Evaluate actual actors, triggers, distinct effects, alternatives and failure cost; simplify default routing first and retire only proven redundant surfaces.
alternatives: Delete all zero-count commands
Treat all CLI calls as skill/model-token telemetry
decisions.rationale: Usage excludes direct APIs and skills. Rare recovery has asymmetric value; compile/clean and expand/replan are review candidates, not established equivalents. Historical counts identify candidate hotspots but need matched current-source evaluation.

decisions.question: How does memory support Exact Context at Right Timing?
decisions.choice: Improve behavior within existing packets, handoffs, decisions, history and source references. Use exact scope filters and a short index before selected detail. Validate the referenced source and relevant contract/environment before reuse; semantic search only proposes candidates.
alternatives: Adopt a general memory platform and second current-state store
Automatically summarize and inject all conversation/tool history
decisions.rationale: Pyramid already persists workflow context. Retrieval, provenance and scoped invalidation address the actual gap without another authority or mandatory service. Unknown and stale facts must stay explicit; no memory entry grants permission or accepts proof.

decisions.question: Which decisions belong in deterministic code?
decisions.choice: Enforce graph completion, coverage links, wire shapes, observed mutation context, exact replan delta and helper reconciliation with pure checks. Keep semantic sufficiency and visual judgments explicit. Apply one risk policy to public changes without treating ordinary authorized work as a new human decision.
alternatives: Add more prompt prose and repeated approvals for mechanical checks
Automatically accept semantic claims based on structural validity
decisions.rationale: The real counterexamples are reproducible relations and identity checks. Machine validity cannot prove user value, review independence or new authority. Existing task owners and cumulative gates cover the fixes without more nodes.

decisions.question: When does a blocker stop other work?
decisions.choice: Return stable reason codes and action scopes for implementation, verification and acceptance. A missing required capability blocks its consumer only. Recompute independent safe work from canonical dependencies, active claims and resources; a batch is not a project-wide barrier.
alternatives: Wait for every batch audit or optional host qualification before selecting any new work
Ignore a failed join or required missing evidence to preserve speed
decisions.rationale: Independent progress and truthful acceptance are compatible. Preserve actual consumed-code dependencies and final composition while avoiding accidental serialization and repeated unchanged approval requests.
